scope: H2 conversational response ownership: bounded sentence streaming, serialized synthesis, immutable origin, actual PCM cancellation and delivery outcomes, connected through both real routers and queued worker. Full application producer/shutdown audit remains pending.

focused.historical_private_flag_tests: Replaced seven synthetic flag/legacy speak assumptions with four actual owner/device/failure/idempotence tests; the remaining multi-room barge-in tests retain their scope

proven: Both real router modes reach the same response handler, native SDK/SSE, real ZoneManager and real StreamingAudioPlayer using synthetic PCM and driver callbacks
A normal conversational response is spoken once and matches all expected PCM frames; a generation failure is announced once and never recorded as a successful conversation
Queued generation returns speech_handled so router delivery depends on actual ownership rather than excluding the SLOW_LLM path
Cached arrays, full-array synthesis, streaming synthesis, earcons and broadcast all use the registered cancelable player and normal drain contract
Slow synthesis does not count as audible output; the is_speaking state starts with the device, while is_responding includes generation/synthesis
Cancelling a blocked synthesis retains its owner slot, prevents a second TTS worker and discards the cancelled old PCM when it finally arrives
A slow consumer bounds the sentence queue at two; cancel wakes a producer blocked on capacity and closes native HTTP resources
Pending response admission is bounded without starting additional synthesis workers
Origin zone remains fixed during waits despite a changed global default; a hook cannot redirect the captured origin and unrelated-zone cancel leaves it running
Unknown zone and missing ZoneManager for an explicit zone fail without playing the default device; unstarted PCM sources close once
Playback failure cancels a pending generation without retrying voice; failed output receipt waits for cooperative cleanup before returning
Sentence splitting preserves a decimal whose point and fractional digits arrive in separate deltas
Accepted captures and barge-in cancel the originating zone; callback/capture code does not perform synthesis or device close
Legacy classifier and vector queries, feedback, confirmations, suggestions, home-action feedback and the HA speak integration use off-loop or managed async delivery
Source-free runtime imports response DTOs/handler and verifies the empty-delivery contract without hardware

checks.chromium: Not repeated; frontend unchanged from prior effect-expansion validation

environment: Existing runtime virtualenv read-only, bytecode writes disabled and GPUs hidden; HTTP/SSE in memory and callback-driven synthetic output
limits: No physical speaker, microphone, amplifier, home service, gateway or GPU model was used; synthetic PCM timing is not acoustic latency or provider performance
Main shares this response handler with both conversational modes, but other direct TTS producers still need a full audit: reminders, routine speech, alerts and announcements
The complete application startup/shutdown graph still needs ownership cleanup and failure/cancellation evidence

Timeout during partial voice delivery and error-announcement ownership need additional connected cases; 180 seconds is an explicit whole-response budget, not an evaluated household latency result or a per-stage deadline design
Existing multi-room barge-in tests and new owned-output tests do not together prove the full main capture-to-cancel graph; that integrated corpus remains pending
A blocking native TTS call cannot be killed by cancelling asyncio; it retains the only owner slot until real exit, and dependency recovery remains H4 work
H0 live home effects/physical MQTT group members and legacy memory treatment remain incomplete, and H3-H6 remain open
Real home control selection stays disabled and production remains unchanged
